Lattice Semiconductor stock stood at USD 122.22 on Nasdaq on September 24, 2026, up 0.46 percent from the prior close. The semiconductor company delivered record Q2 2026 revenue of USD 201.1 million, giving the stock a fresh earnings anchor despite its position 22.2 percent below the 52-week high of USD 157.01.
According to Yahoo Finance, revenue in Q2 2026 rose 62 percent year over year and 18 percent sequentially to USD 201 million. The sequential increase from USD 170.9 million in Q1 2026 shows that the growth was not limited to an easy annual comparison.
The earnings quality was equally important. Non-GAAP EPS reached USD 0.53 in Q2 2026, more than 120 percent above the prior-year level and USD 0.09 above the consensus estimate of USD 0.44, according to Zacks.
Lattice guided to adjusted EPS of USD 0.54 to USD 0.58 for Q3 2026, while revenue guidance stood at USD 245 million to USD 265 million, according to Yahoo Finance. The midpoint of the EPS range is USD 0.56, which would exceed the Q2 result by USD 0.03 if achieved.
Operating leverage is the central financial variable. Standardized Q2 data show operating profit of USD 22.353 million and an operating margin of 11 percent, compared with USD 26.068 million and 15 percent in Q1 2026, so revenue growth has yet to translate into a sequential margin expansion.
Lattice Semiconductor had a market capitalization of USD 16.745 billion as of September 24, 2026, with a 52-week range of USD 60.50 to USD 157.01. The USD 122.22 Nasdaq price therefore sits materially below the yearly high, while the Q3 revenue range of USD 245 million to USD 265 million provides the next concrete test for the growth narrative.

Lam Research stock (ISIN US5128073062) gained 2.17 percent to USD 347.49 on Nasdaq on October 2, 2026, after the company delivered USD 6.72 billion in Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue. The latest move leaves the shares 20.7 percent below their 52-week high of USD 438.50, while the next earnings date is set for October 21, 2026.
According to MarketBeat, Lam Research reported USD 1.82 in EPS and USD 6.72 billion in revenue for its latest quarter, ahead of the USD 1.69 EPS and USD 6.66 billion revenue consensus. Revenue rose 30 percent year over year, and the company set Q1 fiscal 2027 EPS guidance at USD 2.00-2.30.
The June quarter also showed a 52.0 percent non-GAAP gross margin, while fiscal 2026 revenue reached USD 23.23 billion, according to Nasdaq. The comparison matters because the business entered fiscal 2026 with a larger earnings base and stronger demand from memory and advanced logic customers.
On October 1, 2026, B. Riley raised its Lam Research price target from USD 350 to USD 390 and kept a Buy rating, as Markets Insider reported. The new target stands 12.2 percent above the October 2 price, using the target-to-price comparison.
The broader consensus remains Moderate Buy, with an average target of USD 363.14 from 32 analysts, according to MarketBeat. That average is 4.5 percent above the latest Nasdaq price, a smaller gap than B. Riley's individual target and a useful measure of how much optimism is already reflected in the stock.
Lam Research last traded at USD 347.49 on Nasdaq on October 2, 2026, with a session range of USD 344.77 to USD 352.56 and volume of 7,429,457 shares. Market capitalization stood at USD 434.6 billion, while the 52-week range was USD 131.02 to USD 438.50.

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) closed at $347.49 on October 2, up 132.98% over twelve months. Most investors have never heard of the company and could not say what it makes. It builds the machines that carve the patterns into silicon wafers.

What is Lam Research's (LRCX) Economic Moat, and is it Widening or Narrowing?
The Moat is That Nobody Can Afford to Switch:
A chipmaker does not simply buy an etch tool. It spends months tuning a manufacturing process around that specific machine, then qualifies the result with its own customers.
Swapping in a rival tool means repeating all of it and risking the yield on a production line worth billions. Almost nobody does it, which is why these positions last for decades. The returns show what that is worth. Lam earns 37.39% operating margins and converts 31.27% of revenue into net profit on sales of $23.23 billion.
Return on equity is 65.07%. Very few companies anywhere reach that level, and it is the clearest single piece of evidence that the moat is real. Price-to-book of 31.20 tells the same story from another angle. There is barely any physical capital in this business, because what Lam sells is accumulated process knowledge.
DON'T MISS: NVIDIA (NVDA) vs. Broadcom (AVGO): Which AI Chip Stock Has the Stronger Moat?
Widening on Physics, Narrowing on Politics:
The moat is getting wider for a reason nobody at Lam controls. Chips are being built upward rather than outward, stacking more layers to fit more memory in the same area. Every additional layer needs another etch step and another deposition step.
So the number of machines a chipmaker needs rises faster than the number of chips it makes. Revenue grew 30.00% in the most recent quarter on that arithmetic.
